subject: math
title: Mass, Capacity and Metric Units
seo_title: Grade 4 Metric Units Worksheets: Kilo, Centi, Milli, Grams, Kilograms, Millilitres and Litres (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Use metric prefixes to describe the relative size of different metric units, and choose appropriate units and tools to measure length, mass, and capacity
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on metric units: what kilo, centi and milli mean, choosing the unit and tool, grams and kilograms, millilitres and litres, reading scales and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the Ontario curriculum.
key_big: Kilo means 1000: 1 kg = 1000 g. Milli means one thousandth: 1 L = 1000 mL.
key_sub: Compare measurements in the same unit, not just the numbers: 1 kg is more than 900 g. A bigger object is not always heavier.
body_html:
Kilo, centi and milli

Metric units are built from a few base units: the metre for length, the gram for mass and the litre for capacity. A prefix at the front tells you the size.

PrefixMeaningExamples
kilo10001 km = 1000 m, 1 kg = 1000 g
centione hundredth100 cm = 1 m
millione thousandth1000 mm = 1 m, 1000 mL = 1 L

Choose the unit and the tool

Use a benchmark: something you know well. Then pick the unit that gives an easy number.

UnitAbout the same asTool
1 mmthe thickness of a dimeruler
1 cmthe width of your little fingerruler
1 ma big step, or a metre stickmetre stick, measuring tape
1 kmabout 10 soccer fields end to endtrundle wheel, map
1 ga paper clipkitchen scale, pan balance
1 kga 1 L carton of milkkitchen scale, bathroom scale
1 mLa few drops of watermeasuring spoon
1 La carton of milkmeasuring cup, measuring jug

Grams and kilograms, millilitres and litres

1 kg = 1000 g and 1 L = 1000 mL. To change kilograms to grams, multiply by 1000. To change litres to millilitres, multiply by 1000.

Example 1

3 kg 50 g = ☐ g

3 kg = 3000 g. Then add 50 g: 3000 + 50 = 3050.

Answer: 3050 g

Example 2

Which holds more: 1 L or 900 mL?

Use the same unit. 1 L = 1000 mL, and 1000 mL is more than 900 mL.

Answer: 1 L

Read a scale

First find what one mark is worth: the jump between two numbers ÷ the number of spaces. Then count on from the number before the needle.

Bigger is not always heavier

A big beach ball is full of air. A small brick is heavy. Only a scale or a pan balance tells you which is heavier: the lower pan is heavier.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 kg = 100 g or 1 L = 100 mLKilo means 1000: 1 kg = 1000 g. Milli means one thousandth: 1 L = 1000 mL
Thinking 900 g is more than 1 kg because 900 is a bigger numberChange to the same unit first: 1 kg = 1000 g
3 kg 50 g = 350 g or 3500 g3 kg = 3000 g, so 3 kg 50 g = 3050 g
Thinking a bigger object is always heavierCheck with a scale or a pan balance
Thinking a taller container always holds moreFill it and measure: a short, wide bowl can hold more
Counting every mark on a scale as 100 gFind what one mark is worth: jump ÷ spaces

faq.q: What metric units do Grade 4 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum, Grade 4 students use millimetres, centimetres, metres and kilometres for length, grams and kilograms for mass, and millilitres and litres for capacity. They learn what the prefixes kilo, centi and milli mean and choose the best unit and tool.

faq.q: What do kilo, centi and milli mean?
faq.a: Kilo means 1000, centi means one hundredth and milli means one thousandth. So 1 km = 1000 m, 100 cm = 1 m and 1000 mL = 1 L.

faq.q: How many grams are in a kilogram, and how many millilitres are in a litre?
faq.a: There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram and 1000 millilitres in 1 litre. A common mistake is to say 100.

faq.q: What are good benchmarks for 1 gram, 1 kilogram, 1 millilitre and 1 litre?
faq.a: A paper clip has a mass of about 1 g, and a 1 L carton of milk has a mass of about 1 kg. A few drops of water make about 1 mL, and the milk carton holds 1 L.

items.q: In kilometre and kilogram, what does kilo mean?
items.e: Kilo means 1000. 1 kilometre = 1000 metres and 1 kilogram = 1000 grams.

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 m = 1000 mm. (Check: 1 m = 100 cm and each cm is 10 mm: 100 × 10 = 1000.)

items.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so it takes 100 centimetres to make 1 metre: 1 m = 100 cm. A metre stick shows 100 cm.

items.q: Which unit is one hundredth of a metre?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so a centimetre is one hundredth of a metre. A millimetre is one thousandth of a metre.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1000, so 1 kg = 1000 g. Watch out: 1 kg is not 100 g.

items.q: The ribbon is 1 cm long. How many millimetres is that?
items.e: Count the small spaces from 0 to 1: there are 10. Each small space is 1 mm, so 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: In millilitre and millimetre, what does milli mean?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. A millilitre is one thousandth of a litre, so 1000 mL = 1 L.

items.q: How many metres are in 1 kilometre?
items.e: Kilo means 1000, so 1 km = 1000 m. That is about the length of 10 soccer fields.

items.q: Which unit is 1000 times as long as a metre?
items.e: Kilo means 1000, so a kilometre is 1000 metres. A kilogram is 1000 grams: it measures mass, not length.

items.q: In centimetre, what does centi mean?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth. A centimetre is one hundredth of a metre, so 100 cm = 1 m. (Think of a cent: 100 cents make 1 dollar.)

items.q: Which unit is one thousandth of a litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, and litres measure capacity. So a millilitre is one thousandth of a litre.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1000 millilitres make 1 litre: 1 L = 1000 mL.

items.q: Order the units from shortest to longest.
items.e: A millimetre is the tiniest. 10 mm make 1 cm, 100 cm make 1 m, and 1000 m make 1 km.

items.q: Which length is the greatest?
items.e: Change to metres: 1 km = 1000 m, 999 cm is less than 10 m, and 5000 mm = 5 m. 1 km is the greatest even though 1 is the smallest number.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 g is more than 1900 g, 999 g and 850 g. Compare the masses in the same unit, not just the numbers.

items.q: Which capacity is the least?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL and 2 L = 2000 mL. 950 mL is less than 1000 mL, 1200 mL and 2000 mL.

items.q: 3 km = ☐ m
5 m = ☐ cm
7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 7 cm = 7 × 10 = 70 mm.

items.q: A bigger unit gives a smaller number. Which is true?
items.e: Metres are bigger than centimetres, so you need more centimetres: 4 × 100 = 400. 4 m = 400 cm.

sets.title: Choose the unit and the tool

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bag of potatoes?
items.e: A bag of potatoes is heavy to carry. Heavy things are measured in kilograms. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a hockey rink?
items.e: A hockey rink is about 60 m long. Long lengths you can walk are measured in metres.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is short, so a ruler marked in centimetres and millimetres is best.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a loonie?
items.e: A loonie is very light, only about 6 g. Use grams. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the distance from Toronto to Ottawa?
items.e: Toronto and Ottawa are about 400 km apart. Long distances between towns are measured in kilometres.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the distance around your head?
items.e: A measuring tape bends, so it can go around a curved shape. A ruler is stiff and cannot bend.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of an ant?
items.e: An ant is tiny, only a few millimetres long. Use the smallest unit, millimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the width of a math book?
items.e: A book is about 21 cm wide. Use centimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a moose?
items.e: A moose is very heavy, hundreds of kilograms. Use kilograms. Millilitres and litres measure capacity, not mass.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the length of the school hallway?
items.e: A trundle wheel clicks every metre as you roll it, so it is good for long lengths. A 30 cm ruler is much too short.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the thickness of a loonie?
items.e: A loonie is only about 2 mm thick. Tiny lengths are measured in millimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much a juice box holds?
items.e: A juice box holds only about 200 mL. Small amounts are measured in millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, about 150 L. Use litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring 250 mL of milk for a recipe?
items.e: Capacity is measured with a measuring cup or a measuring jug. A scale measures mass.

items.q: Which tool is best for measuring the mass of an apple?
items.e: Mass is measured with a scale or a pan balance. A measuring cup measures capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a crayon?
items.e: A crayon fits in your hand and is about 9 cm long. Use centimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much medicine fits on a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only about 5 mL. Use millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a bit taller than a grown-up, about 2 m. 20 m is as tall as a 6-storey building.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a Grade 4 student?
items.e: A Grade 4 student has a mass of about 30 kg. 30 g is only the mass of about 5 loonies.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a mug of hot chocolate holds?
items.e: A mug holds about a quarter of a 1 L carton, which is 250 mL. 250 L would fill more than a bathtub.

items.q: 2 kg = ☐ g
Half of a kilogram is how many grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Half of 1000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g. (50 g would be half of 100 g.)
1000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1000 are in 7000? 7000 ÷ 1000 = 7, so it is 7 kg.

items.q: Which is heavier: 3 kg or 2500 g?
items.e: 3 kg = 3000 g. 3000 g is more than 2500 g, so 3 kg is heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier: 1 kg or 900 g?
items.e: Change to the same unit: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 g is more than 900 g, so 1 kg is heavier. A bigger number is not always more.

items.q: 5 kg = ☐ g
Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The pan with the brick is lower, so the brick is heavier. The pillow is bigger, but a bigger object is not always heavier.
1000 g = 1 kg, so 5000 g is 5 groups of 1000 g: 5 kg.
1000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1000 are in 3000? 3000 ÷ 1000 = 3, so it is 3 kg.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
items.e: The pan with the jar of jam is lower, so the jar is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. The beach ball is big, but it is full of air.

items.q: Which fact about mass is true?
items.e: Kilo means 1000. One kilogram is 1000 grams.

items.q: 10 kg = ☐ g
2 kg 400 g = ☐ g
3 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: 3 kg = 3000 g. Add the 50 g: 3000 + 50 = 3050 g. Writing 3500 g would add 500 g, not 50 g.
1.5 kg is 1 kg and half a kilogram (5 tenths). 1000 g + 500 g = 1500 g.

items.q: Which mass is the greatest?
items.e: Change all to grams: 1 kg 300 g = 1300 g. 1300 g is more than 1030 g, 1003 g and 130 g.

items.q: Order from lightest to heaviest: 2 kg, 1800 g, 700 g
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. So 700 g < 1800 g < 2000 g. The 2 kg is the heaviest even though 2 is the smallest number.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the pumpkin?
items.e: 500 g + 500 g = 1000 g = 1 kg. Then 2 kg + 1 kg = 3 kg. Do not just add the numbers 2 + 500 + 500: they are in different units.

items.q: How many 250 g packs of butter make 1 kg?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1000. That is 4 packs.

items.q: A teaspoon holds about how much?
items.e: A teaspoon is a good benchmark for 5 mL. 500 mL is half of a 1 L carton of milk.

items.q: 3 L = ☐ mL
A 1 L carton of milk has a mass of about how much?
items.e: 1 L of milk or water has a mass of about 1 kg. So a 1 L carton is a benchmark for 1 kg.

items.q: Which holds more: 4 L or 4500 mL?
items.e: 4 L = 4000 mL. 4500 mL is more than 4000 mL.

items.q: 6 L = ☐ mL
Which holds more: 2 L or 1900 mL?
items.e: 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 mL is more than 1900 mL, so 2 L is more. Compare in the same unit.
1000 mL = 1 L, so 4000 mL is 4 groups of 1000 mL: 4 L.

items.q: Which fact about capacity is true?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1000 millilitres make 1 litre.

items.q: Half of a litre is how many millilitres?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Half of 1000 is 500, so half a litre is 500 mL.

items.q: 10 L = ☐ mL
1 L 250 mL = ☐ mL
4 L 80 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: 4 L = 4000 mL. Add the 80 mL: 4000 + 80 = 4080 mL. Keep the 0 in the hundreds place.
2.5 L is 2 L and half a litre (5 tenths). 2000 mL + 500 mL = 2500 mL.

items.q: Which capacity is the greatest?
items.e: Change all to millilitres: 2 L 50 mL = 2050 mL and 2 L 5 mL = 2005 mL. 2500 mL is the greatest.

items.q: Order from least to most: 1 L, 300 mL, 1100 mL
How many 250 mL glasses can you fill from a full 1 L jug?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1000. That is 4 glasses.

items.q: Leah empties a full 1 L jug into the tall vase A. It fills up, and 400 mL is left in the jug. Then she empties another full 1 L jug into the short bowl B. It fills up, and 100 mL is left. Which container holds more?
items.e: Vase A holds 1000 − 400 = 600 mL. Bowl B holds 1000 − 100 = 900 mL. The bowl holds more. A taller container does not always hold more.

sets.title: Read scales and solve word problems

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers are litres, and 1 L = 1000 mL. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 mL. The top of the water is 1 line above 2 L: 2 L 500 mL.

items.q: How much maple syrup is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 mL. The top of the maple syrup is 1 line above 600: 600 + 50 = 650 mL.
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 3 marks past 400: 400 + 150 = 550 g.

items.q: What mass does the scale show?
items.e: The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1000 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 3 kg + 500 g = 3 kg 500 g.
The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1000 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 400 g = 1 kg 400 g.

items.q: What mass does the scale show?
items.e: The numbers are kilograms, and 1 kg = 1000 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg + 750 g = 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers are litres, and 1 L = 1000 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The top of the water is 1 line above 1 L: 1 L 250 mL.

items.q: The scale shows Priya’s backpack. She takes out a 600 g lunch. What is the mass of the backpack now?
items.e: Each mark is 500 g, so the scale shows 3 kg 500 g = 3500 g. Taking out the lunch makes it lighter: 3500 − 600 = 2900 g.

items.q: Mei wants 2 L of water in the jug for the plants. How much more water does she need?
items.e: Each line is 250 mL, so the jug has 1 L 250 mL = 1250 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1250 = 750 mL more.

items.q: A bag of milk holds 4 L. How many millilitres is that?
A sugar shack fills 4 bottles with maple syrup. Each bottle holds 250 mL. How much maple syrup is that?
Liam’s hockey bag has a mass of 9 kg. He adds his skates, which have a mass of 1 kg 500 g. What is the mass of the bag now?
items.e: Add the kilograms: 9 + 1 = 10 kg. Then add the 500 g: 10 kg 500 g.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 4 campers each carry a 750 mL water bottle. How much water do they carry in all?
items.e: 4 equal groups of 750 mL: 4 × 750 = 3000 mL. That is 3 L.

items.q: A baker has a 2 kg bag of flour. Each batch of muffins uses 250 g. How many batches can the baker make?
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 ÷ 250 = 8, so the baker can make 8 batches.

items.q: Two pumpkins for Thanksgiving have masses of 3 kg 600 g and 2 kg 700 g. What is their total mass?
items.e: Add the grams: 600 + 700 = 1300 g = 1 kg 300 g. Add the kilograms: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 kg. The total is 6 kg 300 g.

items.q: The water cooler at the Terry Fox Run holds 10 L. Each paper cup holds 250 mL. How many cups can be filled?
items.e: 10 L = 10 000 mL. There are 4 cups in each litre (4 × 250 = 1000), so 10 × 4 = 40 cups.

items.q: Amira has 2 L of apple juice. She pours 6 glasses of 300 mL for her friends. How much juice is left?
items.e: The glasses use 6 × 300 = 1800 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1800 = 200 mL left.

items.q: Box A has a mass of 1 kg 800 g. Box B has a mass of 2 kg 200 g. How much heavier is Box B?
items.e: Change to grams: 2200 g − 1800 g = 400 g. (Subtracting 800 − 200 = 600 is the wrong way around.)

items.q: Ava has a big bag of popcorn with a mass of 200 g and a small can of beans with a mass of 400 g. Which is heavier?
items.e: 400 g is more than 200 g, so the can is heavier. The bag is bigger, but bigger does not mean heavier.

items.q: The water jug at the cottage holds 5 L. Aiden uses 1 L 500 mL for cooking and 750 mL for tea. How much water is left?
